memos.headline: S08 and S02 Lead Near Highs; S04 and S09 in Structural Downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market today. S08 sits just 0.3% off its 52-week high with +21.8% over 12 weeks, +13.1% relative strength vs SPY, and RSI at a healthy 62.9—this is the cleanest uptrend in the universe. S02 is similarly strong, up +35.1% over 12 weeks with +26.4% relative strength and only -1.6% from its high, though its +25.1% premium to the 200-day mean makes me slightly cautious about extension risk. On the other side, S04 is -29% from its 52-week high, trading -12.9% below its 200-day mean with persistent negative relative strength (-10.7% over 12 weeks)—this is a broken chart until it reclaims at least the 50-day average. S09 is similarly weak at -19% drawdown, -5.4% below its 50-day, and the worst 4-week relative strength in the universe at -11.9%. S06 is interesting near its highs with low volatility (ATR 2.03%) but its 12-week relative strength is essentially flat, so I have less conviction there than in S08 or S02.

views.note: Strongest trend in the universe: near 52w high, +13.1% 12w relative strength, RSI 62.9 not yet overbought; would reassess on a close below the 50-day (~298).
Massive 12w outperformance of +26.4% vs SPY and only -1.6% from high, but +25.1% above 200d mean raises extension risk; would cut on a break below ~400.
Near 52w high with lowest ATR in the universe (2.03%) and +8.8% 4w return, but flat 12w relative strength tempers conviction; invalidated below ~315.
+66.3% 26w return and +34.3% above 200d mean is parabolic, but RSI has cooled to 49.8 and it's -10.6% from high—trend is up but risk of mean reversion is elevated with 5% ATR.
Strong 1w bounce of +8.3% but still -10.5% from high and flat 12w relative strength; needs to clear the prior high to confirm.
Sitting -4.2% below 50d mean with RSI 47 and weakening 4w relative strength of -3.8%; trend is ambiguous until it reclaims the 50-day.
Flat on its 50d mean but -12.1% from high and -6.9% 12w relative strength; no edge either way, would need a break above ~155 or below ~140 to act.
Middling RSI 50.9 and -10.2% 12w relative strength suggest underperformance despite modest 26w gain; no clear setup.
Down -29% from 52w high, -12.9% below 200d mean, negative returns across all timeframes—classic broken downtrend; would reconsider only above ~405 (50d reclaim).
Worst 4w and 12w relative strength in the universe (-11.9% and -15.7%), RSI 44.3, and -19% drawdown; trend is clearly down until it reclaims the 50-day (~147).

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 Margin Collapse Is a Red Flag
memos.body: I am most convicted on the top-line and margin durability at S10 and S05. S10 posted $81.6B in revenue (+85% YoY) with a 71.5% net margin and only $8.5B in total debt—this is the cleanest earnings profile in the universe. S05 delivered $110B in revenue (+22% YoY) at a 57% net margin on just $14.8B of debt, with net income up 81% YoY, suggesting powerful operating leverage. On the other end, S09's net income fell 46% YoY to $4.2B on essentially flat revenue (+2.4%), compressing net margin to just 4.9%—I need to see margin stabilization before getting constructive. S02 is similarly sluggish at +2% revenue growth and a thin 5.6% margin with $77.9B in debt, offering no earnings catalyst. S04 and S03 are solid growers (revenue +18% and +17% respectively) but S04's 38% margin and lower leverage make it the more attractive of the two.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, 71.5% net margin, minimal debt of $8.5B—best earnings power and balance sheet in the universe.
Net income +81% YoY to $62.6B on a 57% margin with only $14.8B debt; durable high-margin compounder.
Revenue +18% YoY, 38% net margin, and manageable $40B debt; net income growth of 23% shows solid operating leverage.
Revenue +17% YoY and net income +77% are encouraging, but 16.7% margin and $123B in debt leave less room for error—need to see margin expansion sustain.
Revenue +22% and net income +27% are healthy, but 14.6% margin and $36B debt on $17B revenue imply high leverage; would upgrade on margin improvement.
Solid 27% margin and +17% revenue growth, but $83B in debt is heavy; earnings growth of 19% needs to outpace interest costs.
33% net margin is attractive but $449B in total debt dwarfs $50B revenue; any rate or credit stress would compress earnings quickly.
Net income collapsed 46% YoY to $4.2B on flat revenue, margin at just 4.9%—clear cash-flow compression with no visible inflection.
Revenue +2% YoY, net income flat at $6.3B, 5.6% margin, and $78B debt—no earnings catalyst and thin margin of safety.
Modest +7% revenue growth and 18.5% margin are respectable but unexciting; $24B debt on $21B revenue warrants monitoring.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% but Sticky 4.2% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Favor Banks Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see a clear pause regime: the Fed has held the upper bound at 3.75% for three months while CPI is running at +4.2% YoY, well above target, which makes further cuts unlikely near-term and a hike scenario non-trivial. The 10y yield has climbed 25bp over three months to 4.56%, and the 10y-2y spread has compressed 13bp to +0.38pp, signaling the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates. The labor market is resilient with unemployment at 4.20%, down 10bp over three months, which removes any urgency for the Fed to ease. I have conviction that this environment punishes long-duration growth equities and benefits banks (positive curve, elevated short rates boosting NIM), while staples face margin pressure from sticky inflation. A CPI print falling below 3.5% YoY or unemployment rising above 4.5% would shift my regime call toward easing and reverse these sector tilts.

views.note: Rising long yields and a pause regime pressure duration-sensitive growth names via higher discount rates.
Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve at 38bp and elevated short rates supporting net interest margins in a pause regime.
Cyclicals face mixed signals: solid labor market supports demand but sticky inflation and rising yields cap multiples.
Staples face margin compression from 4.2% YoY CPI with limited pricing power upside and no rate-cut tailwind.
Energy is a partial inflation hedge but curve flattening and demand uncertainty from a potential slowdown keep me neutral.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds as the 10y yield rises 25bp in three months with no easing catalyst in sight.

memos.headline: S09 Delisting/Acquisition Cluster and S05 Governance Overhaul Stand Out in Otherwise Routine Filing Season
memos.body: I am reading the 8-K filing cadence across the universe as a proxy for narrative intensity, since no GDELT tone data was provided. S09 filed a heavily loaded 8-K on 2026-07-01 covering an acquisition completion, delisting notice, bylaws amendments, and board changes—this is the single most event-dense filing in the universe and signals a major corporate transformation that likely shifts sentiment sharply. S05 has the highest filing volume (five 8-Ks in three weeks) including material definitive agreements, rights modifications, and multiple officer changes, suggesting an active restructuring narrative. S03 shows steady activity with a new financial obligation on 2026-06-10 and two 'Other Events' filings including one just yesterday (2026-07-09), keeping it in the news flow. S10's earnings-related 8-K on 2026-05-20 drew a -1.8% price reaction, and the subsequent board change on 2026-07-02 may be a lagged response—tone here looks like it bottomed and could be stabilizing.

views.note: Delisting notice and acquisition completion on 2026-07-01 create extreme uncertainty; sentiment is likely very negative and not yet fully absorbed.
Five 8-Ks in three weeks including material agreements and officer turnover suggest active restructuring—narrative is shifting but direction unclear.
Post-earnings -1.8% reaction on 2026-05-20 likely priced the bad news; subsequent board change may signal a tone inflection from trough.
Steady filing cadence including a new financial obligation and fresh 'Other Events' filing on 2026-07-09 keeps narrative active without negative catalysts.
Six filings over five weeks including Reg FD disclosure and officer changes are moderately active but lack a clear directional catalyst.
Only a single officer departure/appointment filing on 2026-06-05; too little information flow to form a sentiment view.

memos.headline: Collapsing Oil Prices and Falling VIX Signal Easing Geopolitical Risk Premium, but Policy Uncertainty Remains Elevated
memos.body: I note that WTI crude has dropped 26.6% over three months to $73.15/bbl, a move consistent with either demand destruction or a meaningful de-escalation in energy-supply geopolitical risk — either way, this removes a tailwind for energy-exposed names and eases input costs for energy consumers. The VIX at 15.84 is down ~20% over one month, suggesting markets are pricing out near-term conflict or sanctions shocks, yet the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 282.56 is still elevated and ticked up 2% month-over-month, which tells me structural policy risk (export controls, China decoupling, tariff posturing) has not resolved. High-yield OAS at 2.70% and tightening confirms credit markets are sanguine, but I would need to see the EPU index break below 250 to gain conviction that the policy overhang has truly cleared. Without detailed 8-K content for the universe names, I am relying on macro signals and filing frequency — S06's four filings in under a month suggest active corporate repositioning that could be policy-related, warranting closer monitoring.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in a month including Reg FD disclosures suggest active repositioning, possibly around regulatory or policy developments, but without content detail I cannot take a directional view.
Two 8-K Other Events filings in a month and the still-elevated EPU index keep me on the sidelines until I can assess whether these disclosures relate to sanctions or supply-chain shifts.

Falling oil prices (-26.6% over 3 months) and tightening credit spreads are broadly supportive for non-energy corporates; Reg FD disclosure in June may signal proactive investor engagement ahead of improving macro backdrop.
Single 8-K filing and no specific geopolitical catalyst; the benign VIX and credit environment are supportive but elevated policy uncertainty keeps me from adding risk here.
Reg FD disclosure in June and the sharp drop in oil prices reduce energy-cost headwinds; VIX decline supports risk-taking, though I would reverse on any new export-control escalation.
No company-specific filings in the evidence set and while macro conditions are improving, the persistent EPU elevation warrants caution absent direct geopolitical clarity.
